content:
Let \(r^{3n-9}=2\). Then \(r=2^{1/(3n-9)}\).

Substitute into the correct all-terms product:
\[
2^{n/3}r^{(n^2-3n)/2}=64.
\]
So
\[
2^{n/3}\left(2^{1/(3n-9)}\right)^{(n^2-3n)/2}=2^6.
\]
The exponent of \(2\) is
\[
\frac n3+\frac{n^2-3n}{2(3n-9)}
=\frac n3+\frac{n(n-3)}{6(n-3)}
=\frac n3+\frac n6
=\frac n2.
\]
Thus
\[
2^{n/2}=2^6,
\]
so \(n=12\).

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
